intro: A plate of mee kicap is about 450 kcal (estimate). Most of the calories come from the yellow noodles, oil and the sweet soy sauce mixed in.

breakdown.part: Oil, kicap manis and dark soy sauce
A little chicken or char siu, plus vegetables

diet: Yes, but watch how often and how much. Mee kicap is mostly carbs and fairly low in protein, so you get hungry again quickly. Once in a while is okay, especially if you add protein and vegetables. For everyday meals, soup noodles are usually lighter.
tips: Ask for 'less oil, less kicap' when you order.
Add vegetables plus a boiled egg or extra chicken so you stay full longer.
Get a small portion, or eat half the noodles and finish the protein.

swap.name: Mee sup ayam
swap.why: Less oil and sweet soy sauce. The soup fills you up, and you still get protein from the chicken.

faq.q: What's the difference between mee kicap and mee goreng?
faq.a: Mee kicap is usually tossed or lightly cooked with soy sauce. Mee goreng is stir-fried with spices and sauces, and is usually oilier.

faq.q: Is kicap manis high in sugar?
faq.a: Yes, kicap manis has quite a lot of sugar. Ask for less, or mix it with light soy sauce.
A little, but they're mostly carbs. Your main protein should come from chicken, egg or other toppings.
